questions.q: What are the three real parts every for loop needs, per this lesson?
options: A start condition, a middle condition, and a step
Only a condition — start and step are optional
A contract name, a function name, and a return type
A mapping, a struct, and an array
questions.explain: The instructor was explicit: you need a starting condition, a condition in the middle, and a step condition for something to count as a valid for loop.

questions.q: What does `continue` actually do when it runs inside a loop?
options: Skips the rest of the current iteration and jumps to the step, moving to the next value
Pauses the contract until manually resumed
questions.explain: continue skips whatever code comes after it in that one iteration and jumps straight to the loop's step, continuing with the next value.

questions.q: What does `break` actually do when it runs inside a loop?
options: Skips just the current iteration and continues the loop
Has no effect inside a for loop
questions.explain: break stops the loop completely — once it runs, no further iterations happen at all.

questions.q: In the real while loop example, what is the default value of `j` before the loop starts?
options: 0, since unassigned Solidity variables always default to zero
It causes a compile error to leave it unassigned
questions.explain: j is declared without an initial value, and Solidity variables that are unassigned always default to zero — confirmed and explained live in class.

questions.q: What real structural difference does a while loop have compared to a for loop?
options: A while loop has no built-in start/condition/step structure — you manage the increment yourself inside the loop body
A while loop can never use a condition
A while loop always runs exactly 10 times
There is no real difference at all
questions.explain: Unlike a for loop's three-part header, a while loop only checks a condition — you're responsible for incrementing the variable yourself inside the loop body.
